title: Test local reconstitution and inherited reasoning in isolation
problem: GREG has local transport repair and a directed construction path. The missing evidence is useful reasoning formed by local interaction and retained for later work.
baseline: The recorded MICA/CDPE transport parity and the incremental central reasoning arm on the new fixture.

alternatives.name: Adaptive central
advantages: Simple exact recovery on these fixtures.
disadvantages: A coordinating component is required in the model.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retain as the active comparison and prefer it if it continues to win.

alternatives.name: Frozen local links
alternatives.description: Same local operators with original links preserved.
advantages: Separates rewiring from effects of the operators.
disadvantages: Cannot select an alternate provider after loss.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retain as an ablation until a better isolation design exists.

alternatives.name: Adaptive local links
alternatives.description: Local receivers bind matching offers and export a role preference from an observed proof.
advantages: Recovery can happen by local reactions.
disadvantages: Polling and extracted preference may cost more than they return.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Repeat with dormant alternatives, an event-driven arm and hidden transfer.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Keep existing repair and Genesis; the transfer hypothesis stays untested.
disadvantages: No contrast between reasoning repair and transport repair.

roles.position: Keep emergent and inherited reasoning as the target; label local rerouting a precursor.
material_concerns: A known backup can make recovery look like new competence.

roles.position: Exercise typed offers and live proofs in the existing isolated evaluation surface.
material_concerns: Local polling can cost more than an incremental central evaluator.

roles.position: Require frozen-edge, adaptive central and cold controls, plus a separate evaluator; a known backup does not establish generation.

roles.position: Use synthetic data and cost and provenance checks; qualified runtime work remains separately governed.
material_concerns: A one-position preference may be equivalent to a static rule.

evidence.finding: The local arm recovered and the frozen control did not.

evidence.claim: A learned preference applies to another authored domain
evidence.finding: All five proofs agree; the inherited arm makes zero rather than one rewire.

counterevidence.finding: Three checks for central closure; local checked five by first answer and 30 across its observation phase.

counterevidence.claim: Transfer had no speed or rule-check gain
counterevidence.finding: Both arms reached the main target at round three and used 36 checks.

pass_1.intended_outcome: Recover a proof with partial loss and measure whether an extracted arrangement helps on a new task.

advantages.amplified_value: Pair identical operators with frozen connections and retain the failed arm.

disadvantages.statement: A known backup can make recovery look like new competence.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Keep provenance and compare a frozen-network control; state whether the alternate was available already.

comparisons.do_nothing: Preserves history and leaves the question open.
comparisons.reversible_experiment: Synthetic test program with an independently prepared transfer case.

rejected_alternatives.name: Direct runtime attachment
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Predeclared advantage against matched strong alternatives, canonical approval and integrated replay.

pass_2.attack_summary: Attack mislabeled transport repair, route memorization, and central advantage under normal execution.

new_weaknesses.statement: A one-position preference may be equivalent to a static rule.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Freeze code before a separate agent supplies a different dependency shape; keep a static corroboration policy for the successor comparison.
